title: Teaching his sister's piano piece and picking out tunes
summary: He showed his sister a piece at her lesson; the teacher told his mother he was getting free lessons, but there was no money, so he taught himself by ear at about ten.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: horn. It didn't make any difference, you know. And so that knocked me out there and back to when my mother was sending me to lessons with my sister, I got so sick and tired of listening to my sister make mistakes and I went up there and played it for her. I said, "This is the way this goes," and I played it for my sister and the teacher was in the back room, you know, she had some beans on, cooking beans. She went to see about her beans. So she hollered, "Now, that's the way I've been trying to get you to do that all the time." She come back in there and she said, "Now, do that again." Sister said "I didn't do it," she says, "he did."

Her name was Mrs. Aires. So she looked at me, she says, "You did that?" I said, "Yes." She said, "All right, do it again." So I did. So she said, "Okay." She sent my mother a note. She says, "Don't send this boy with these girls to take their music lessons anymore, because he's getting a lesson free."
So, well, you know what I mean.

But she did in the meantime finally told my mother, she says, "I'll tell you what." She said, "You're spending your money foolishly. The girls don't care anything about it. I'm going to tell you. Give that boy lessons."

But you know, my mother, you know how some people feel, she says, "Oh, this boy will never use it. He'll never do this. He'll never do that." And she says, "Well --" "And we don't have the money." So she just, you know -- so finally, I would sneak up to the piano and start picking out things, you know, start picking out little things on the piano.
Like how old would you be here, ten?
I'd say about ten, 11, you know, start picking out a few little things, and then --
Not from notes — you couldn't read.
